candidate_relations.reason: The label prioritizes necrotizing fasciitis (NF) as the working diagnosis in this gas-forming labial infection, matching the reference object.
Pyoderma gangrenosum is a neutrophilic ulcer without subcutaneous gas or sepsis physiology.
Fournier gangrene is necrotizing fasciitis of the perineum/genitalia, the same disease at this labial-groin site.
Gas gangrene/clostridial myonecrosis is a related gas-forming NSTI but specifies muscle clostridial infection rather than fasciitis.
Staphylococcal scalded-skin syndrome is a superficial exfoliative toxin disease, not deep necrotizing infection.
Flesh-eating disease is a colloquial alias for necrotizing fasciitis.
Perineal abscess is a localized suppurative differential and lacks the necrotizing fascial process.
Vulvar cellulitis is the non-necrotizing soft-tissue infection and conflicts with gas in the abdominal wall.
Hypotension and leukocytosis indicate sepsis as a physiologic state, not the tissue diagnosis.
Abscess is a possible coexisting collection, not necrotizing fasciitis.
Cellulitis is the incompatible non-necrotizing counterpart.
Streptococcal toxic shock can accompany NF but is a toxin-mediated shock syndrome, not the fascial diagnosis.
Ecthyma gangrenosum is typically Pseudomonas septic embolic skin necrosis, not this labial NSTI.
Necrotizing cellulitis is a related NSTI confined more superficially than fasciitis.
Meleney gangrene is postoperative progressive bacterial synergistic gangrene, a different named NSTI.
Necrotizing soft-tissue infection is the parent category of necrotizing fasciitis.
Considering cellulitis names the incompatible milder diagnosis rather than necrotizing fasciitis.
Necrotizing myositis targets muscle rather than fascia.
None does not identify necrotizing fasciitis.
Clostridial myonecrosis is gas gangrene of muscle, not fascia-centered NF.

case_quality_flags: Labial ulcer with subcutaneous gas prompted surgery for necrotizing infection despite a low initial LRINEC score.
